issue.title: Deck block rail and panel chrome subscribe to theme_changed_signal without unsubscribing, pinning removed widgets

task_type_fields.impact: Every deck block rail or panel chrome that is removed (deck rebuilds, layout operations, panel swaps) stays in memory for the TUI session unless the theme changes. That is a slow leak in the long-lived `sase tui` process.
task_type_fields.repro: Proposed by sase-1es.8 (note #4) and confirmed on master 702c8c3167. `src/sase/ace/tui/widgets/decks/panel_chrome.py:42` (`_subscribe_theme_changes`) and `src/sase/ace/tui/widgets/decks/block_rail.py:554` (`on_mount`) call `self.app.theme_changed_signal.subscribe(self, self._on_app_theme_changed)` and never call `unsubscribe`. Neither file defines `on_unmount` or contains `unsubscribe`. Textual's Signal keeps callbacks as values of a WeakKeyDictionary keyed by the subscriber, so the bound-method value strongly references its key. An unmounted widget therefore stays reachable from the App, with everything it holds, until a theme change prunes it. Epic sase-1es fixed this exact leak in the pager (src/sase/pager/view.py on_mount/on_unmount, 8d1ac50c51) and gated it with tests/pager/test_view_leak.py. Fix: call `self.app.theme_changed_signal.unsubscribe(self)` in `on_unmount` (wrapped in try/except like the pager), and add a weakref/gc leak test that mounts and removes each widget.

issue.creation_reason: Epic sase-1es fixed this exact Signal WeakKeyDictionary leak in PagerView and flagged two ACE deck widgets with the same subscribe-without-unsubscribe pattern.
